thread:
maria: heads up — since 09:02 UTC we have a sustained throughput drop on the dedicated pool dc-prod-us-west1. Errors from a handful of customers (429s) and p95 latency jumped from 180ms -> ~650ms. Queue depth looks elevated but autoscaler hasn't added nodes. Anyone oncall/near the runtime? :eyes:

sam_ops: on it, pinging metrics and autoscale logs. do we have a ticket from the customer?

dena_support: customer ticket #7894 — they report repeated 429s between 09:05-09:22. Said they didn't change request rate. attaching their sample request ids.

kevin_ml: quick signal — continuous-batcher avg batch token count dropped ~30% in the last 15m, but I also see `max_batch_tokens` at 5120 for that pool. If per-request token lengths decreased, we can get more microbatches and scheduling overhead. pulling scheduler traces.

maria: useful, thanks. autoscaler window looks normal though?

sam_ops: from autoscale logs: `scale_event suppressed: queue_threshold_not_crossed (current_queue=48, threshold=50)` at 09:10. But queue depth later hits 120 and still no scale — I see repeated `throttle_policy=tenant_limits` logs around 09:14.

deploy-bot: [09:12] autoscaler-controller: evaluated pool=dc-prod-us-west1, desired=12, current=12, pending=0, scale_suppressed=true, reason="recent_scale_failure"

kevin_ml: oof, "recent_scale_failure" flag is sticky for 10m by default if prior attempts hit provisioning failures. but that shouldn't block urgent scale. maybe a bug where we only clear on successful reconcile. pulling kube events.

ellis_sre: checking node provisioning events — got an error 09:08-09:09: `quotaExceeded: insufficient vram capacity in us-west1-zone3` which caused scale attempt to fail. After that, controller set `scale_backoff`. That explains suppression. However cluster-level isn't the only path: we should fall back to routing policy (burst into other region) which didn't happen; routing logs show requests stayed pinned.

maria: pinned by dedicated pool assignment for that customer. They have SLA-backed capacity, so we can't route them away. That means failing scale attempts will cause sustained throttles.

kevin_ml: back to batching — scheduler traces show many small microbatches being scheduled (batch sizes 1-3) even though there were enough queued tokens to form larger batches. Looks like scheduler windowing was shortened by an earlier config change: `sched_max_wait_ms` lowered from 20 -> 2ms in canary yesterday. That would reduce batching opportunity.

sam_ops: can you paste the trace snippet?

kevin_ml: sure:
```
[09:07:50] batch_window_start id=0 tokens_queued=600
[09:07:50] create_microbatch id=0 size=2 tokens=96
[09:07:50] execute_microbatch id=0
[09:07:50] create_microbatch id=1 size=1 tokens=20
[09:07:50] create_microbatch id=2 size=1 tokens=12
[09:07:50] ... wasted scheduling overhead, many exec calls
```

kevin_ml: the scheduler was chopping because of the 2ms window. If we revert to 20ms OR increase `max_batch_tokens` to allow larger batches, it should improve throughput. But note autoscale still needed.

ellis_sre: got it. immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert sched_max_wait_ms to 20ms on dc-prod as a hotfix for the runtime config (will trigger rolling config reload), 2) temporarily relax scale_backoff to allow immediate retry, 3) open capacity request with cloud for vram quota to avoid future provisioning failures.

maria: can we do 1 and 2 now? which steps are safe for customer SLA?

ellis_sre: step 1 is low risk — config reload is non-disruptive and only affects scheduling. Doing that now. Step 2 needs infra approval (relaxing backoff) but I can apply a short-term override in controller for this pool.

sam_ops: I'll coordinate the override with infra and watch for new scale events. kevin, can you run a quick load-run on staging with the same sched_max_wait_ms=2 -> 20 change to verify?

kevin_ml: running a synthetic workload now on staging to reproduce microbatch starvation. using `siege-proto` ramp to match customer token size distribution. Will post results in ~7m.

deploy-bot: [09:20] config-reload: runtime-config service applied to pool=dc-prod-us-west1, sched_max_wait_ms=20

kevin_ml: staging run: before change p95 throughput 120 req/s, after change p95 throughput 168 req/s and avg batch token count increased by 45%. Good signal.

dena_support: I contacted the customer and told them we're working on autoscale and scheduler tuning; they appreciate the update.

maria: great. sam, keep an eye on 10m window. if throttle rate for that pool doesn't drop below 1% by 09:40 escalate to incident. I'll update the ticket.

sam_ops: watching. I'll also add a temporary alert for `autoscaler.suppressed == true AND queue_depth > 80` so infra can get an automated heads-up next time. :+1:

ellis_sre: note for postmortem: stickiness of `scale_backoff` plus sched_window change = compounded impact. we'll capture exact timelines.

maria: thanks team. summary: root cause = failed scale attempt (quota) made controller suppress further autoscaling; config change to sched_max_wait_ms lowered batching efficiency and amplified queueing; mitigation = revert sched window, force a controller override to retry scaling, request vram quota. owners: ellis (infra/controller), kevin (repro + perf), sam (monitoring/alerts), dena (customer comms). :white_check_mark:

sam_ops: confirmed throttles dropped to <0.8% after the changes and p95 latency trending down to ~220ms. closing for now, will follow up in postmortem. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
